alexandre-alex-monteiro.text: Priorities include expanding first-time homebuyer programs and advocating "for affordable and workforce housing so residents can live and work in Hawthorne."

source.title: Re-Elect Alex Monteiro for Hawthorne City Council 2026 (campaign site)

alexandre-alex-monteiro.text: Says he helped develop Hawthorne Tiny Homes as temporary housing for unhoused residents until permanent placement, and grew SBCCOG homeless funding for Hawthorne from $40,000 to $500,000 a year.

alexandre-alex-monteiro.text: Says he secured a $6 million SBCCOG Housing Trust soft loan for the Cordary Adobe project, 92 low-income units.

source.title: Alex's Accomplishments 2018-2026 - Alex Monteiro for Hawthorne (campaign site)

alexandre-alex-monteiro.text: Supported Hawthorne PD technology including surveillance cameras, drones and aircraft policing, plus community policing programs; priority to "strengthen public safety while building trust between residents and law enforcement."

alexandre-alex-monteiro.text: Says he is committed to "fighting for good-paying jobs with benefits" and college and vocational career pathways.

alexandre-alex-monteiro.text: Endorsed by the LA County Democratic Party, IBEW Local 11, LA County Firefighters IAFF Local 1014, Hawthorne Municipal Employees Association and Rep. Maxine Waters.
